angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 5,409,068 km at 75.30 pc = 0.96 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 103527: distance 75.301 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.023), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 75.301 +/- 1.732 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 13.3021 +/- 0.0652 mas (same row, RUWE 1.08), 204.1 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 7.775 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 103527: radius 7.775 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 34.488 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.055) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 5,409,068 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5020 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 103527: effective temperature 5020 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.037) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 103527: effective temperature 5020 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.037) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of 18 Del (pscomppars): spectral type G6 III, from Teng et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023PASJ...75.1030T/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of 18 Del (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.06 dex, from Teng et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023PASJ...75.1030T/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of 18 Del (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 1.63367, from Teng et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023PASJ...75.1030T/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of 18 Del (pscomppars): age 1.1 Gyr, from Baines et al. 2009 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009ApJ...701..154B/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * 18 Del: projected rotation speed 3.97 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2025A&A...704A..49B)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 3.08 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 17 published values span log g 2.84 to 3.3, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...683A.125P)
